In this field, armature matters because the form the mask is built on It is taught at the Advanced level of the teaching ladder, building from first principles toward professional practice, with each concept defined before it is used.
overview: Mask Making is the field concerned with making masks: plaster, papier-mache, and foam techniques The Future of Mask Making belongs to its essential core. Concretely: Armature — the form the mask is built on And Ventilation — breathing holes and eye openings planned before finishing Mastering this entry means being able to explain the topic in plain sentences, recognize it in real cases, and apply it alongside the neighboring ideas of the Advanced tier.
core_concepts: Armature: the form the mask is built on
Ventilation: breathing holes and eye openings planned before finishing
key_laws: Seal porous surfaces before painting or the paint soaks in.
Fit matters: an uncomfortable mask never gets worn.
vocabulary: Release agent: the barrier (like petroleum jelly) letting plaster leave the skin
Thermoplastic: heat-shapeable plastic for durable masks
methods: Plaster method: apply release agent, lay damp bandage strips, set 20 minutes, remove and finish
